title: Woolworths Limited - proposed acquisition of Packaged Liquor licence in Erina NSW
targets: Packaged Liquor licence in Erina NSW

timeline.event: ACCC commenced review under the Merger Review Process Guidelines.
Closing date for submissions from interested parties.
ACCC announced it would not oppose the proposed acquisition.

body_sections.Summary: On 3 March 2009 Woolworths advised the ACCC that it proposes to acquire a dormant packaged liquor licence in Erina, NSW.
body_sections.Market definition: The ACCC took the view that the relevant markets in this matter were likely to be: 1.  The local market for the retail sale of liquor for off-premises consumption, with a geographic dimension of 3-5km surrounding the target liquor outlet. (Market 1) 2.  A NSW market for the wholesale supply of packaged liquor for subsequent sale in the retail market for off-premises consumption. (Market 2)
body_sections.Competition analysis: On 17 March 2009 the ACCC formed the view that the proposed acquisition would be unlikely to substantially lessen competition in the relevant markets. Factors informing this conclusion were: Market 1 The ACCC considered that Woolworths would likely continue to be constrained by a number of other retail liquor outlets in the relevant market. In addition, the proposed acquisition would not lead to the removal of a vigorous and effective competitor as the licence is currently dormant. Market 2 The ACCC considered that the proposed acquisition would not significantly increase the buying power of Woolworths or substantially diminish the buying power of any competing wholesaler in the relevant market.
